question.text: Which of the following correctly describes an Indian Depository Receipt (IDR)?

answer.text: An instrument denominated in Indian Rupees created by a Domestic Depository against underlying equity shares of a foreign company
A receipt issued by a foreign depository bank representing shares of an Indian company
A government security denominated in foreign currency issued in India
A derivative instrument linked to the performance of international indices

explanation.text: The Logic: An IDR is an instrument denominated in Indian Rupees, in the form of a depository receipt created by a Domestic Depository against the underlying equity shares of a foreign issuing company. Foreign companies can raise capital from the Indian markets by issuing IDRs, with two-way fungibility permitted. The Trap: Option B describes the reverse direction (an Indian company's shares represented abroad by an ADR/GDR), not an IDR. Note: Pages 19 and 36-37 support the rupee-denominated IDR definition and the two-way fungibility point; the dollar-denominated ADR/GDR comparison is not stated in the pages checked.
